messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-usw2-pool-42' p99 latency breach (SLO: 500ms) — p95=1.9s p99=6.8s. Queue depth=278, warmup timeouts=42, errors=rate-limited/502. See metrics: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/graphs/pool-42
sarah (oncall): acknowledged. paging eng-sre + runtime. oncall taking lead. I'm on call for the next 45.
mike (eng-sre): looking. initial glance: autoscaler logs show multiple failed handshakes to pool nodes, scale-up requests queued ~40s behind target. suspect ASG scaling lag + warmup window mismatch. grabbing logs now.
lina (eng-runtime): runtime shows heavy KV cache coldpath vs usual. many requests hitting cold L0 -> warmup path. warmup latency for model-gpt-medium ~250ms cold, but we are seeing 1.2-3s per warmup due to many concurrent inits.
support-alex: support telemetry shows 3 customers reporting streaming stalls and client timeouts (~10m) — CS ticket ids: #CS-7713, #CS-7720, #CS-7726. they're seeing mid-stream stalls and eventual 502 after retry.
cs-rita: flagged top customer (acme-ads) — revenue impact, their prod traffic routed to Dedicated. They have a large batch of short chats hitting tail latency.
mike (eng-sre): here's the key log snippet from autoscaler:
```
2026-02-11T10:02:39Z autoscaler: request scale-up pool=42 desired=8 current=4
2026-02-11T10:02:39Z autoscaler: create-instance attempt=1 rc=ERR_HANDSHAKE timeout=30s
2026-02-11T10:03:20Z autoscaler: retries left=2 backoff=15s
2026-02-11T10:03:40Z autoscaler: instance-ready id=i-0a1b2c warmup=2.4s
```
Looks like handshakes are stuttering under load.
ankit (oncall-next): can we temporarily route lower-priority traffic to hosted fallback? also consider manual scale of pool to short-circuit autoscaler.
lina (eng-runtime): we can enable prefix-KV cache warmup in hotshot mode for this pool, but it will take ~30s to populate. Alternatively drop small-burst batch size to reduce per-request latency, trade throughput.
mike (eng-sre): performing manual scale now: `redwoodctl dedicated scale --pool dedicated-usw2-pool-42 --replicas 8 --reason "emergency-scale-autoscaler-lag"`
deploy-bot: Scaling request accepted. starting 4 new nodes for pool dedicated-usw2-pool-42. estimate warmup 120s.
sarah (oncall): good. while nodes come up, can we throttle background jobs and deprioritize embedding-only requests? those amplify queue.
lina (eng-runtime): started low-priority eviction policy for embeddings: set `evict-priority=low` on pool-42 -> now. That should free ~15% queue capacity.
triage-bot: NOTE: temporary routing rule created -> route low_priority -> hosted-backup-usw2.
mike (eng-sre): autoscaler telemetry shows handshake error rate dropping after manual scale commands, but warmup latencies still high due to model coldstarts. Patch: set `preload=true` on new nodes to prefetch weights; initiating.
incident-bot: Service update: p95 now 1.0s, p99 2.6s (was 1.9s / 6.8s). queue depth -> 92. Errors falling.
support-alex: CS update sent to affected customers: initial mitigation applied, we routed lower-priority traffic to hosted fallback and scaled pool manually. waiting on customer confirmation.
cs-rita: acme-ads confirmed reduced errors, still seeing a few stalls but much improved. they asked for ETA on full mitigation.
ankit (oncall-next): I'm taking over the channel at +30. Summary for handoff: root cause suspected autoscaler handshake/backoff under burst; warmup/COLD cache increased tail latencies; manual scale + evict low-priority traffic + hosted fallback applied. Next steps: postmortem, extend autoscaler handshake timeouts? or make warmup proactive.
sarah (oncall): agreed. action items: 1) eng-sre to capture full autoscaler trace + backoff params (mike), 2) runtime to document preload options and add a warmup budget (lina), 3) ops to add runbook checklist for manual scale + routing (ankit), 4) CS to follow up with customers (cs-rita).
mike (eng-sre): saving logs to /var/incidents/1768881234/autoscaler-trace.log and uploading to S3: s3://incidents/1768881234/autoscaler-trace.log
lina (eng-runtime): I'll experiment with reduced batch size for streaming path in canary (deploy change id: canary/stream-batch-20260211). moving config.
triage-bot: REMINDER: create postmortem ticket and link to this thread.
sarah (oncall): handing off to @ankit (oncall-next). final note: system stabilized; p99 dropped to 800ms after new nodes warmed up. If anything spikes again, please @sarah and escalate to paging.
ankit (oncall-next): acknowledged, taking ownership. I'll monitor next 2h and coordinate the postmortem. adding action items to board.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (stabilized). Close after 2h of stability or manual confirmation.
cs-rita: adding customer follow-ups and credits as needed.
support-alex: closing CS tickets once customers confirm.
ankit (oncall-next): quick notes for handoff doc: suspected contributing factors: bursty PLG onboarding traffic, autoscaler backoff too conservative under transient failures, warmup budget too low for model size. Proposed short-term fixes: bump autoscaler retries, add proactive preload, ephemeral hotshot pool for onboarding bursts, improve backlog shedding for low-priority requests. Long-term: capacity planning for burst SLAs + autoscaler improvements.
sarah (oncall): thanks everyone. will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow. :pray:
